videos.title: VoiceOver sigue abriendo puertas. Phonon trae nuevas voces a la conversación
videos.description:
VoiceOver continúa ampliando sus posibilidades, y hoy le toca el turno a Phonon, una aplicación que permite incorporar nuevas voces al lector de pantalla de Apple.
En este tutorial conoceremos cómo funciona Phonon, cómo explorar las voces disponibles, seleccionar las que nos interesan, descargarlas y utilizarlas con VoiceOver.
Todo explicado paso a paso, con demostraciones prácticas para que puedan escuchar las voces y valorar cuáles se ajustan mejor a sus preferencias.
Porque cuando hablamos de accesibilidad, tener más opciones para elegir siempre es una buena noticia.

videos.title: ¿Una galería de fotos pensada para personas ciegas? Así funciona Memora
videos.description:
Memora: ¿para qué quiere una persona ciega una galería de fotos?
¿Quién dijo que las fotografías son solamente para quienes pueden verlas?
Hoy les presento Memora, una aplicación para iPhone desarrollada por un programador ciego que propone una forma accesible de explorar y organizar nuestras fotografías.
En este tutorial recorreremos sus principales funciones, comprobaremos cómo se maneja con VoiceOver y veremos qué posibilidades ofrece en la práctica.
Una nueva oportunidad para demostrar que la accesibilidad también tiene mucho que decir en el mundo de la fotografía.
TifloAcosta. Tecnología al alcance de todos.

videos.title: Apple te quiere… proteger. ¡Pero tienes que activarlo! iOS 27
videos.description:
Apple quiere protegernos de las estafas, y con iOS 27 incorpora una nueva función llamada «Detección de riesgo de suplantación de identidad».
¿En qué consiste? ¿Puede nuestro iPhone detectar que alguien está intentando engañarnos para conseguir nuestro dinero o nuestros datos personales?
En este vídeo de TifloAcosta explico cómo funciona esta protección, cuáles son sus limitaciones y cómo podemos activarla desde los ajustes del iPhone utilizando VoiceOver.
Una novedad importante que viene desactivada de fábrica y que necesita aplicaciones compatibles para funcionar. No evita todas las estafas, pero puede aportar una protección adicional.

videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.
Tony Acosta
Canal TifloAcosta

Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.

La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.

En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.

videos.title: Actualizaciones invisibles en iPhone: qué son y por qué importan
videos.description:
Apple no solo actualiza el iPhone cuando aparece una nueva versión de iOS. Existe un sistema menos visible que trabaja en segundo plano y que mucha gente no conoce: las actualizaciones rápidas de seguridad y datos del sistema.
Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.
Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.
En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.
videos.fullDescription:
Apple no solo actualiza el iPhone cuando aparece una nueva versión de iOS. Existe un sistema menos visible que trabaja en segundo plano y que mucha gente no conoce: las actualizaciones rápidas de seguridad y datos del sistema.

Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.

Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.

En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.

news.title: LiDAR en los teléfonos móviles: una tecnología que podría ayudar a las personas ciegas a detectar escaleras y desniveles
news.summary: Los avances en tiflotecnología no siempre requieren desarrollar nuevos dispositivos. En ocasiones, el potencial está en aprovechar tecnologías que ya incorporan herramientas de uso cotidiano, como los teléfonos inteligentes. Es el caso del sistema experimental desarrollado por investigadores de la Universidad de Iowa (Estados Unidos), que utiliza el sensor LiDAR de un teléfono móvil para […] La entrada LiDAR en los teléfonos móviles: una tecnología que podría ayudar a las personas ciegas a detectar escaleras y desniveles se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
Los avances en tiflotecnología no siempre requieren desarrollar nuevos dispositivos. En ocasiones, el potencial está en aprovechar tecnologías que ya incorporan herramientas de uso cotidiano, como los teléfonos inteligentes.

Es el caso del sistema experimental desarrollado por investigadores de la Universidad de Iowa (Estados Unidos), que utiliza el sensor LiDAR de un teléfono móvil para detectar escaleras y cambios de altura en el terreno en tiempo real.

La investigación, publicada el 2 de octubre de 2026 en la revista científica Scientific Reports , demuestra que es posible utilizar el sensor de profundidad de un smartphone comercial para identificar determinados riesgos durante los desplazamientos, sin necesidad de incorporar cámaras externas ni hardware especializado.

LiDAR es una tecnología que permite medir distancias y obtener información tridimensional del entorno mediante pulsos de luz láser.

Algunos teléfonos inteligentes, como determinados modelos de iPhone Pro, incorporan sensores LiDAR que permiten detectar la profundidad de los objetos y construir representaciones tridimensionales de los espacios.

Aunque esta tecnología se utiliza habitualmente en fotografía, aplicaciones de realidad aumentada y mediciones de espacios, también ofrece posibilidades interesantes en el ámbito de la accesibilidad.

En este caso, los investigadores han aprovechado esa capacidad para identificar irregularidades en el suelo, especialmente escaleras y cambios de altura que pueden pasar desapercibidos durante los desplazamientos de una persona ciega o con baja visión.

El sistema desarrollado utiliza un iPhone 17 Pro Max con iOS 26.2 y el sensor LiDAR integrado en el dispositivo.

Su funcionamiento se basa en analizar la representación tridimensional del entorno que genera el teléfono. A partir de esa información, un algoritmo proyecta ocho líneas virtuales en diferentes direcciones para identificar cambios geométricos en la superficie.

Cuando detecta una variación compatible con una escalera o un desnivel, el sistema puede generar una alerta para advertir al usuario.

Una de las características más interesantes es que el procesamiento se realiza directamente en el teléfono, sin necesidad de enviar las imágenes a servidores externos ni utilizar procesamiento en la nube.

El algoritmo analiza la información a una frecuencia de 60 imágenes por segundo, lo que permite detectar cambios en el entorno con una respuesta prácticamente inmediata.

Para comprobar el funcionamiento del sistema, los investigadores realizaron 120 pruebas en ocho ubicaciones diferentes, utilizando escaleras con distintas alturas y pendientes.

Los ensayos contemplaron diferentes condiciones de iluminación, tanto en interiores como en exteriores, y aproximaciones a las escaleras desde arriba y desde abajo.

Los resultados fueron los siguientes:

Los investigadores también observaron diferencias según la dirección de aproximación. La detección fue menos eficaz cuando el usuario se acercaba a las escaleras desde arriba, algo especialmente relevante porque los desniveles descendentes pueden resultar difíciles de identificar mediante sensores de profundidad.

Es importante interpretar estos resultados con cautela: las pruebas fueron realizadas por un único operador entrenado y no incluyeron participantes ciegos o con baja visión. Además, no se llevaron a cabo ensayos específicos en recorridos sin obstáculos para establecer una tasa de falsas alarmas fiable.

Por tanto, los resultados demuestran la viabilidad técnica del sistema, pero todavía no permiten afirmar que esté preparado para su utilización autónoma en situaciones reales.

Una de las ventajas de esta investigación es que no requiere desarrollar un dispositivo completamente nuevo.

El sistema aprovecha un sensor LiDAR que ya está integrado en determinados teléfonos comerciales. Esto abre la posibilidad de explorar aplicaciones de asistencia visual utilizando hardware que algunas personas ya tienen a su disposición.

No obstante, es importante señalar que no todos los smartphones incorporan LiDAR. Además, el algoritmo desarrollado depende de las características del sensor y del entorno de programación utilizado, por lo que no puede trasladarse automáticamente a cualquier teléfono.

Los investigadores consideran necesario ampliar las pruebas, incorporar diferentes dispositivos y evaluar el funcionamiento del sistema con personas ciegas y con baja visión antes de plantear su utilización como herramienta de movilidad.

La detección de escaleras y desniveles continúa siendo uno de los desafíos de la movilidad para las personas con discapacidad visual.

Aunque el bastón blanco es una herramienta fundamental para detectar obstáculos y explorar el espacio próximo, determinadas situaciones pueden requerir información adicional sobre las características del terreno.

La utilización de sensores de profundidad en teléfonos móviles podría abrir nuevas posibilidades para complementar las ayudas técnicas existentes, proporcionando información adicional sobre el entorno y anticipando determinados riesgos.

Sin embargo, estas tecnologías todavía necesitan demostrar su fiabilidad en condiciones reales y no deben considerarse sustitutas del bastón blanco ni de la formación en orientación y movilidad.

La investigación demuestra que los sensores LiDAR de los teléfonos inteligentes tienen un potencial que va mucho más allá de la fotografía y la realidad aumentada. Su aplicación en el ámbito de la tiflotecnología podría contribuir al desarrollo de herramientas más accesibles, económicas y fáciles de integrar en dispositivos cotidianos.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

news.title: Apple's new research app is designed to make AI health tools more user-friendly
news.summary: Apple has unveiled a new research study with the aim of learning how people use AI health tools.
news.body:
It will allow users to ask health questions and rate the responses.

Apple has unveiled a new research study with the aim of learning how people use AI health tools in order to make them more effective and user-friendly. The company is launching the Health AI Usage Study in conjunction with OpenEvidence , a clinical AI platform used by health professionals that draws medical data from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine .

A key part of the research is a new app now available for download , with Apple aiming to have up to 200,000 participants. Users must live in the US and be 21 or older, and have an iPhone 15 Pro or later model running iOS 26 and up. They can choose to share (or not) Apple HealthKit data, including activity levels, sleep quality and lab results, for extra context around their health.

Participants will use the app to ask medical questions via text-based prompts like "how can I improve my heart health," according to the app's screen shots. They'll then receive non-jargony responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources. Apple's goal is to use the data to create AI health tools that deliver relevant, easy-to-understand and actionable health information.

Apple notes that the app is not integrated with Siri or Apple Intelligence, and said that participant data will remain confidential and won't be used to train AI models.

"[We] believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding," said Apple VP of Health and fitness Sumbul Desai, MD, in a statement. "Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey."

news.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
news.summary: Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions
news.body:
Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people.

The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.

The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys.

Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues.

Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.

“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”

The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week .

news.title: The oldest gadget in your house could be your home network's biggest security hole
news.summary: It may be more economical to hold onto gadgets for as long as possible, but you're putting your entire home network at risk with outdate hardware.
news.body:
Your home network is only as secure as its weakest link.

It may not seem like you would need to replace a perfectly functional 10-year-old connected camera in your home. However, your network is only as secure as its weakest link, and that's often a device that is so outdated it no longer receives updates from its manufacturer.

Many of us don't realize how often gadgets need to be replaced, and it's not just cameras. Security cameras should be replaced every five to seven years, with router manufacturer Netgear recommending a hardware replacement every four or five years. You'll know it's well beyond time to replace your router when you start experiencing slower connections. At that point, you may already be facing security concerns.

When outdated gadgets like these are compromised, they could be sending your data to bad actors or working as part of a botnet. In 2025, the FBI issued a warning that end-of-life (EOL) routers–devices that are no longer receiving software updates or security patches–are being compromised by cybercriminals. It's ultimately up to the consumer to perform a regular device audit to determine if routers, cameras and other smart devices pose a security risk.

Any connected device in your home that no longer receives bug patches and security updates may be a risk. Per a 2024 Consumer Reports study, most appliance makers don't tell consumers in advance how long they will offer updates to software. It found that of 19 major brands that make smart appliances, only three told customers how long they would maintain support, and even the longest promised about five years of updates, falling short of consumer expectations of 10.

Routers are also often at risk. A 2025 FBI warning stated that routers dated 2010 or earlier likely no longer receive updates and should be replaced. In this particular case, such gadgets were being targeted by malware called TheMoon, which infects routers to install proxies, so criminals can operate anonymously. TheMoon hack doesn't even require a password, instead exploiting open ports and a vulnerable script. Even if you have a strong password, an old router can be a risk.

Routers and other smart devices that have been hacked can be recruited as part of a botnet, a network of devices used to overwhelm websites with traffic to take them offline. A recent report from Cisco found that nearly 40 percent of the vulnerabilities attackers targeted most affected end-of-life devices, and about a third of exploited vulnerabilities were at least a decade old. The report focused on businesses, but the lesson applies at home too: Attackers keep targeting old hardware because it never gets fixed. Even if most of your cameras and routers are up to date, just one outdated device can allow bad actors to enter the network and compromise anything else connected to it.

The good news is you don't have to replace everything in your home. Start by taking stock of everything on your network. First, log into your router's admin page and go through the list of connected devices. You may find gadgets you have forgotten about, like an old camera, smart plug or even your fridge. Then, search online for whether the manufacturer still releases updates for each device. If your router no longer gets firmware updates or is considered an EOL gadget, it may be time to get rid of it. If your smart appliance is too old to get automatic updates, you can simply turn off connected features. Chances are you don't need them anyway.

The latest standard for router security is WPA3. To upgrade your router from WPA2, go to the router's admin page, find the wireless security setting and choose WPA3. Some older gadgets will struggle to connect after switching, so choose WPA2/WPA3 if you run into that issue. If there is no WPA3 option, it is time to replace the router.

To make your home network more secure in general, turn off remote management and use a strong password. Never use the default password that came with your router. Turn on automatic updates to ensure firmware is updated as soon as it is offered. Otherwise, you can put any old gadgets and smart appliances on a separate network so that, if they are compromised, they can't get to more important gadgets like your laptop or phone. It's worth noting, though, that the data stored on outdated gadgets is still vulnerable, so it's always best to replace old hardware for maximum security.

news.title: The pros and cons of using cloud storage over local storage
news.summary: Before AI ran rampant through the technology market, cloud storage was the new, big thing, as it seems like every major company has its own cloud service.
news.body:
Cloud storage can be super convenient, but there are times when using local storage is the better move.

External hard drives and USB flash drives are usually easy ways to back up your files, especially since they don't require an internet connection or waiting for uploads. You just plug them into your computer, copy the files you need, and that's it. But cloud services like iCloud and Google Drive have also made it a lot easier to back up everything — and most of the time, it all happens automatically.

Your photos, videos, contacts and more are all synced to the cloud without having to copy each file manually. Plus, there's no risk of leaving your external drive somewhere or damaging it to the point where you lose your files . That doesn't mean cloud storage is perfect, and both have their pros and cons — it really comes down to choosing what works best for your needs. If you're unsure whether to choose local or cloud storage to back up your data, here's how the two stack up on access, cost and reliability.

One of the biggest advantages of using cloud storage is the convenience of not having to worry about your files. Once you upload them to the cloud, they're with you wherever you go. Just log in to your account on another laptop or phone, and you can access everything in just a few minutes. It's perfect for people who use multiple devices or who need to access files from their home computer at the office or college. Plus, most cloud services let you have your files synced automatically . That's the case with iCloud — once you enable it on your device, it automatically backs up everything every day.

Sharing files through a cloud service is also much easier than sharing them from local storage. Once a file is uploaded to the cloud, you can easily share it with someone with just a click — cloud platforms generate a link so others can view and download that file. There's also collaboration, so multiple people can work on the same document or spreadsheet at the same time. Platforms like Google Docs even offer tools that allow each collaborator to leave comments in real time, perfect for workplaces and schools.

Safety is another big plus, since major cloud providers keep copies of your data spread across multiple servers and data centers. The chances of something bad happening and you losing all your data are very low – though not impossible . Plus, your cloud account can be protected with a password and two-factor authentication, meaning others can't just take your files from you.

Cloud storage relies on a stable internet connection, and you're prone to unexpected outages. A slow connection or an outage on your provider's servers could prevent you from downloading a file when you need it most. Also, uploading and downloading large files can take a while if you're using a slow connection. With an external SSD, you can copy gigabytes of files in just minutes. Internet has no impact on local storage, so it's something to consider if you're always traveling and rely on mobile data, for example.

Cost is another reason that might push people away from cloud services. While you only have to pay once to buy an external hard drive, cloud providers typically charge recurring subscription fees on a monthly or annual basis. Apple charges $9.99 per month in the US for 2TB of iCloud+ , which comes to nearly $240 if you pay for two years — and the storage isn't really yours. Stop paying, and your files may be deleted after a while, not to mention possible price increases down the road . By comparison, you can find 2TB SSDs for around $290, but they'll always be yours, with no extra charges.

That doesn't mean you should ditch the cloud and rely entirely on local storage. Subscribing to a cloud service that allows you to back up all your files and access them from anywhere is very handy, and you can also benefit from local storage by offloading some of your larger files or those you really want to make sure you never lose.

news.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
news.summary: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics.
news.body:
Bharat Semi , an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere.

The investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027.

India has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets.

The New Delhi-based startup is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing, and AI capabilities on a single chip, reducing the need to send visual data to separate processors. The move could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional setups that use a separate image sensor, image signal processor, and a system-on-chip, co-founder Vrinda Kapoor (pictured above, right) said in an interview.

“Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions,” Kapoor told TechCrunch.

Kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow who earlier worked in healthcare technology, co-founded Bharat Semi in late 2021 with Vinayak Dalmia (pictured above, left), the startup’s managing director, who previously worked at McKinsey and in private equity. Its chief technology officer, Boyd Fowler, previously held the same role at image-sensor maker OmniVision.

Bharat Semi is targeting smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance, and aerospace. Without disclosing specifics, Kapoor pointed to air conditioners that could detect when a room is empty and adjust automatically and drones that could process visual information — even with the absence of more expensive computing hardware elsewhere in the system.

The startup’s first-generation sensors are already in prototyping, while its second-generation sensors, which will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities, are expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, Kapoor said. Moreover, the startup plans to get those newer sensors into customers’ hands by the end of 2027.

The all-equity seed round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors. Bharat Semi, Kapoor said, plans to use the funding to expand its engineering team, complete product development, and bring its sensors to market.

Bharat Semi has about 75 employees across India and the U.S., including 10 to 12 in its American operations, which span engineering and business development in Santa Clara. The startup plans to increase its U.S. headcount to around 20 by mid-2027, Kapoor said. It has also begun hiring engineers in Europe.

“It’s a story of can we build a global technology company out of India,” Kapoor said.

In 2024, Bharat Semi announced plans for a semiconductor fabrication project in India involving a technology partnership with the U.S. Space Force. The initiative, Kapoor said, remains in development and the startup is working to identify domestic partners that would build and operate the facility.

The project is separate from Bharat Semi’s image-sensor business, Kapoor added. The startup plans to remain fabless, outsourcing chip manufacturing while focusing on semiconductor design and software. The new funding will not be used to finance the proposed fabrication facility.

news.title: Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?
news.summary: "Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia."
news.body:
We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.”

“Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.”

Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return .) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem.

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity; you can listen to the whole episode here .

Tim De Chant: I figured this was coming. I didn’t think it would happen this quickly. I thought there would be at least a few days.

Rebecca Bellan: I didn’t think it was going to happen at all. I mean, Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia. And we’ve got nothing but the last few years of data to show us that billionaires can do whatever the hell they want. So it was surprising to me — it almost restored my faith in humanity, that he resigned.

But someone said to me, “If this were Elon, nothing would happen.” He would not be resigning. Nothing would be going down

Anthony Ha: Which is interesting, because I would have said, as of a week ago, or even just a few days ago, that Jensen is in the same category as Elon. I mean, no one is quite as special as Elon is, but it’s a big, incredibly successful company. Like you said — in a lot of ways, the entire AI economy is built on top of Nvidia.

And for most people, Jensen Huang is Nvidia. He’s the biggest shareholder. He has family members who work at the company, and probably most importantly, there was no succession plan in place. So this was not something that they were prepared for at all.

Rebecca: I think we should actually take a step back, because we just launched into this conversation assuming — rightly so — that our listeners will know what the heck we’re talking about.

But for those who somehow don’t, Jensen resigned on Thursday, after it came out he was having an affair with a former executive at an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, who’s alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. And then there was another reported affair with an Nvidia executive.

So he’s resigned. Nvidia CFO Collette Kress is jumping in as the interim CEO. She’s a longtime board member. I think it’s always interesting when a CFO steps in to be a CEO. It just means we’re going to manage expenses right now, like that’s the key.

Anthony: I think a big part of the message is: This is not necessarily someone you should expect to be in this role for the long term. No disrespect to her, but it feels like a caretaker appointment while they figure things out.

Just to get into that backstory a little bit more, what has been really remarkable to me has been this sense that a lot of what ultimately brought Huang down, [that] stuff was at least known in intelligence circles for a while. Apparently, this report that [raises] questions, concerns about his relationship with Alice Huang is something that was circulating a year ago, or close to a year ago.

And then suddenly, everything really accelerated, Starting over the weekend, with Jensen Huang admitting to having an affair, the board saying it was investigating, but that it still had a lot of faith in him. And then this week, this other affair being reported on, and it just felt like there was all this bad news coming fairly quickly.

But also, it wasn’t this thing that no one had known before. I guess a lot of the general public hadn’t known. So it’s this combined feeling of, “Wow, the ground kind of shifted so quickly under him,” even though the worst stuff, the possibility that somehow national security might have been threatened, is something that actually has been known by the government for nearly a year, if not more.

Rebecca: That’s exactly right. Trump was given some warnings about Huang’s affair with someone who has ties to Chinese intelligence, potentially, and it seemed like he didn’t really mind.

I think what’s important here, though, is to note that Jensen Huang has been an advocate for loosening chip exports to China. And so this is where the crux of it is. Can anyone trust him as the CEO of this company when he’s advocating for loosening chip exports to China? Which a lot of people believe is a national security issue, because that means it will give Chinese AI companies access to our powerful chips, which will help them improve their AI, which could threaten America.

I mean, there’s two sides of this coin. And I think, honestly, that Jensen does not need a woman to tell him that — he just wants to sell more chips, and to anybody and everybody, and whether or not that’s good for national security or not, I think is honestly secondary to him.

Tim: I completely agree. I think the big turning point seems to happen on November 9 — so that would have been earlier this week, Monday, when the Bloomberg report came out and suggested that Nvidia’s head attorney had some role in inquiring about the Department of Commerce’s investigation into Alice Huang.

Things seem to have accelerated in the last few days following that. And I don’t know what role exactly that report played in it, but it seems to be maybe there was a shift within government or within the board, a kind of a daunting realization of the extent to which this had spread just beyond Jensen and some affair.

Anthony: There’s also just the question of: What does this mean for Nvidia? What does this mean for the broader AI industry? And one of the reasons those two things are very tightly connected is not just Nvidia chips themselves, but also the fact that under Jensen Huang, the company has invested very, very heavily in a number of AI startups.

People talk about the idea of an AI circular economy, and I think Nvidia has been one of the biggest players in that, in terms of both funding a lot of things, [but] also, obviously, providing the infrastructure for a lot of AI projects. So if Nvidia is going into this stage of lockdown, circle the wagons — even if it just means a small pullback, that could have really dramatic repercussions.

Rebecca: Yeah, that’s what I want to know: What happens to the Bank of Nvidia without Jensen? Is he the one leading this?

Just to throw some numbers at you, Nvidia apparently accounts for roughly 80% of the AI GPU market. It reported $99 billion in investments and another $25 billion in commitments, plus $36 billion dollars in cloud service commitments. A lot of those include investments into CoreWeave, Nebius, OpenAI, Anthropic, major data center projects. They’ve got their fingers in literally everybody’s pie.

news.title: Apple engineers ‘actively working’ on Face ID for iPhone Duo 2’s outer display: report
news.summary: Next fall, Apple will introduce its second-generation iPhone Duo. It’s unclear what it’ll offer in terms of meaningful upgrades outside of the usual chip upgrades and camera improvements, but Apple engineers are reportedly attempting to bake Face ID into the device. That said, the feature might not make the cutoff. more…
news.body:
Next fall, Apple will introduce its second-generation iPhone Duo. It’s unclear what it’ll offer in terms of meaningful upgrades outside of the usual chip upgrades and camera improvements, but Apple engineers are reportedly attempting to bake Face ID into the device. That said, the feature might not make the cutoff.

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman , Apple has two priorities for iPhone Duo: Face ID and the Action Button. The latter might just end up being a new software addition to Camera Control that allows you to remap the hold action from Siri in Camera to an app of your choice.

As for Face ID, Apple engineers are ‘actively working’ on integrating the technology on the device, specifically on the outer display:

Other goals for the next couple of generations include adding a telephoto camera and making the device thinner and lighter overall. But Face ID is the top priority. I’m told that Apple has already developed prototypes of the iPhone Duo 2 with Face ID, and engineers are still actively working to integrate the facial-recognition system into the outer display of the second-generation model.

That said, the feature might not make it. According to Gurman, the timelines are tight here and it isn’t quite ready – so he isn’t reporting with certainty on whether or not this feature will make it. If it doesn’t debut with the iPhone Duo 2, it’ll likely be in the cards for iPhone Duo 3 in 2028.

Later down the road, the company wants to introduce an improved camera system for the iPhone Duo, including a telephoto camera. It also wants to make the device even thinner and lighter. The Duo definitely needs to be lighter, but making it even thinner would be an interesting feat.

While Face ID on the iPhone Duo would certainly be much appreciated, I’m not quite convinced that it’ll be super meaningful on only the outer display.

I’m fine with Touch ID, but whenever it is bothersome, it’s usually on the inner display, where it can be hard to reach the button depending on how you’re holding the device. If I could only have Face ID on one display, I think I’d rather have it on the inner display.

Orientation can make a huge difference for how you reach Touch ID on the inner display, whereas you’re generally only going to hold the outer display one of two ways: upright in your left hand, or upright in your right hand.

news.title: Apple’s Siri AI smart glasses are reportedly launching next year, here’s what to expect
news.summary: Apple’s long awaited smart glasses, akin to Meta Ray-Bans but tailored to Siri AI and the Apple ecosystem, are almost here. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman , the product should be introduced at the next WWDC, and they should be on the market by the end of the year. Here’s what to expect. more…
news.body:
Apple’s long awaited smart glasses, akin to Meta Ray-Bans but tailored to Siri AI and the Apple ecosystem, are almost here. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman , the product should be introduced at the next WWDC, and they should be on the market by the end of the year. Here’s what to expect.

First and foremost, Apple wants to rely on its deep app ecosystem to give its glasses a boost. While companies like Meta are undeniably leading in the agentic AI assistant game, the third party app integration just isn’t quite there.

Starting with iOS 27.3 beta, Apple is finally l aying the groundwork for proper third party app integration within Siri, rather than just Siri Shortcuts. By the time the glasses release at the end of next year, there should be a plethora of third-party integrations to utilize.

That said, the glasses themselves won’t run apps directly. Everything will rely on a nearby iPhone, per Gurman . The glasses will still have Wi-Fi for apps to function if an iPhone isn’t nearby, but these will largely serve as an iPhone accessory.

According to the report, Apple’s glasses will likely be slightly thinner than a pair of Meta Ray-Bans :

In terms of industrial design, internal prototypes are slightly thinner than Meta’s second-generation Ray-Ban glasses. At least on some test units, the cameras are housed in oval-shaped openings that sit flush with the frame — rather than protruding from it. There’s also a light on the front that shows when the glasses are in use or charging. Apple has been experimenting with other features on the front of the glasses related to privacy.

Lastly, a big focus of these glasses is the audio quality. According to Bloomberg , engineers are describing the audio quality as “industry-leading.”

news.summary: PLOT is interactive fiction written by AI. Pick a genre, or write one line about the story you want, and the AI writes a scene.…
news.body:
Published 15 November 2026 by KihaKwon

PLOT is interactive fiction written by AI. Pick a genre, or write one line about the story you want, and the AI writes a scene. At the end of each scene you choose one of two options or type what happens next, and the story keeps going for as long as you like.

You can keep several stories going at once. Sign-in options include Google, Apple, Kakao, or a 6-digit email code. The app and stories are available in 40 languages.

PLOT is free with optional in-app purchases. You receive 30 pages at sign-up, can earn up to 49 additional one-time pages from first-step activities in the app, and can earn up to 17 pages per day through daily check-ins and small tasks. Optional short video ads can provide 3 pages each, up to 10 times per day. One page equals one scene.

One-time page packs are also available for purchase. There is no subscription and no banner advertising.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Disclosure: I’m the developer (Mirror Lab). I’ve used PLOT with TalkBack and my eyes closed on my Galaxy S25, for a long time last summer and again after 2.0. Just before 2.0.0, the main flow was also tested on a Galaxy S23 running Android 16, from sign-in to Get pages. No step got stuck.

PLOT follows system font size up to 200%, bold font, high contrast text, and remove animations. PLOT does not read aloud by itself.

Version 2.0.1 fixes these three issues and was in Google Play review in November 2026. The keyboard fix requires Android 15 or later. Video ads have not yet been checked with TalkBack.

Feedback is welcome, including workarounds you may have found. Contact contact@plotai.app , or use Profile > Settings > Feedback & support in the app.

news.title: AcessGallery
news.summary: AcessGallery is a photo and video gallery built from the ground up for blind and low-vision people who use a screen reader. Instead of simply…
news.body:
Published 14 November 2026 by Marco Rafael

AcessGallery is a photo and video gallery built from the ground up for blind and low-vision people who use a screen reader. Instead of simply announcing “Image” and a date, it uses AI to describe what is in your photos, narrate what happens in your videos, read text found in pictures, and answer your questions about any image.

The app also works as a complete gallery, with albums, a photos/videos filter, and support for Android’s “Open with” option. There are no ads and no account to create. The AI features use the Google Gemini API and can be enabled in two ways: with your own free API key, which is stored only on your device, or with the optional Facilitator plan, a monthly subscription for people who cannot or prefer not to create a key.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

I am the developer of AcessGallery. The app was designed for screen reader users from the start and every screen was tested with TalkBack. All buttons and controls have descriptive labels, state changes—such as a description finishing or a filter being applied—are announced, and touch targets are large to make them easy to find and activate.

With TalkBack, you can move through your photos and videos with standard gestures, double-tap a photo, and then ask for a description, have its text read aloud, or ask a question about it.

To use the AI features, you can create a free Gemini API key in Google AI Studio and paste it into the app’s settings. Since this setup can be difficult for less experienced users, the Facilitator plan offers a simpler alternative: subscribe and the AI features work right away, with no key to create or configure.

The AI features require an internet connection, and images are sent for processing by Google’s Gemini service. Face detection runs entirely on the device.

news.title: Easy Voice
news.summary: Easy Voice is a free text-to-speech routing app for Android. It does not synthesize speech itself; instead, it sits between Android and the TTS engines…
news.body:
Published 14 November 2026 by Syed Sharib Ali

Easy Voice is a free text-to-speech routing app for Android. It does not synthesize speech itself; instead, it sits between Android and the TTS engines already installed on the device, routing text to the engine best suited to the detected language and selected mode.

Dual Languages Mode uses a primary and secondary language, routing Latin-script text through the primary language and matching non-Latin text to the configured secondary engine.

Auto Language Mode can use as many configured languages as needed and sends each complete block of text to a single matching engine.

Mixed Mode processes words and languages with their own configured TTS engines, making it better suited to content that frequently switches languages.

Easy Voice also includes advanced options for smart number processing, punctuation handling, quick character reading, accessibility-volume output, and Keep Alive behavior.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Setting up Easy Voice takes only a few minutes. Follow these steps:

The Configurations tab gives you detailed control over every language. You can enable, disable, or remove languages at any time. There is also a checkbox that invokes the corresponding TTS engine immediately, with no delay. This is especially useful when a TTS engine supports only one language.

The Advanced tab offers several options for tuning how Easy Voice behaves:

news.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
news.summary: Airlines praised the AI tool, but the air traffic controllers’ union wasn’t involved.
news.body:
The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment.

“After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.

news.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
news.summary: Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.
news.body:
How do you think you're going to die?

If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident."

In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.

news.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
news.summary: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
news.body:
Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.

On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.

news.body:
Have you ever opened a photo and wanted to know right away who’s in it, or spot the dog in the corner, or see what’s on the dinner plate? If you use magnification, you know how that usually goes. You zoom in, pan across the picture bit by bit, and hope you don’t miss what you’re looking for. It works, but it takes time and patience.

Photo Tracking, new in ZoomText 2027, makes this much easier. Instead of scanning every corner of an image, you can go straight to the things that matter to you. Let’s take a look at what it does and how to get started.

Photo Tracking identifies people, animals, food, and other objects in an image. Then it moves the magnified view directly from one object to the next. You no longer need to zoom and pan across the whole picture to find what you want. Photo Tracking takes you right to it.

Photo Tracking is available in ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText Magnifier, and Fusion.

Pictures are everywhere: on web pages, in Word documents and PDFs, and in your own photo collection. Photo Tracking helps you get to the parts of an image you care about quickly, so you spend less time searching and more time enjoying or using what you find.

There’s another big benefit. All recognition happens locally on your computer. That means Photo Tracking works offline, and it’s suitable for secure environments where images can’t be sent to an online service.

Getting started takes just a few steps:

Tip: You can also set Photo Tracking to analyze the active window automatically.

Photo Tracking sorts the objects it finds into ten categories:

It starts with your favorite categories, which are Animals and People by default. If you’d rather start somewhere else, you can change your favorites in Photo Tracking Settings.

Use these keystrokes while you explore an image:

When you zoom in or out with CAPS LOCK+UP ARROW , CAPS LOCK+DOWN ARROW , or CAPS LOCK+ENTER while using Photo Tracking, ZoomText announces the new magnification level, so you always know where you are.

For complete hotkeys and settings, see the Photo Tracking help topic in ZoomText. To learn more about Photo Tracking and other ZoomText 2027 features, visit What’s New in ZoomText 2027 .

Give Photo Tracking a try the next time you come across a picture. We think you’ll enjoy how quickly you can find what you’re looking for.

news.title: In-Process 13th November 2026
news.summary: This week, we’ve updated NVDA, and some documentation, we hear from our user group in Japan, plus there are tips for File Explorer and more! NVDA 2026.3.1 Updated VPAT / ACR NVDA on show in Japan Unassigned gestures File Explorer shortcuts NVDA 2026.3.1 NV Access is pleased to announce that version 2026.3.1 of NVDA, the… Read More
news.body:
This week, we’ve updated NVDA, and some documentation, we hear from our user group in Japan, plus there are tips for File Explorer and more!

NV Access is pleased to announce that version 2026.3.1 of NVDA , the free screen reader for Microsoft Windows, is now available for download. We encourage all users to upgrade to this version.

Highlights This is a patch release to fix security issues. A bug fix is also included for an issue introduced in 2026.3 with the task switcher in Windows 10. The Brazilian Portuguese eSpeak voice was restored to the behaviour in 2026.2.

Read the full changes and download at the NVDA 2026.3.1 release announcement .

We’ve updated our VPAT. Actually we’ve updated our ACR , but whatever you call it, there’s a new one. Mostly of interest to companies who use NVDA and need to keep a copy on file for any software they use, the activity of completing it is useful, even for us as a screen reader manufacturer. VPAT stands for Voluntary Product Accessibility Template – it’s a large document which gives you points to consider and rate your software and website on many aspects of accessibility. VPAT is technically the blank template. The Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) is the completed report about a product.

NVDA is, as you would expect, quite good at all the things someone who is blind might need. However, through this process, over the years, we have previously identified and fixed several issues which may affect other users. The newest version of this document doesn’t dramatically change any of our ratings or identify or fix any new issues, but it is up to date for NVDA 2026.3.1. So, if your organisation needs a copy, head over to the VPAT section of the Corporate and Government page and you’ll find it there.

We love to hear from our communities all around the world. There is a very active community of users, and contributors in Japan. They have a website devoted to the local community: https://www.nvda.jp/ and recently attended the Sight World 2026 conference in Tokyo https://www.sight-world.com/sightworld2026

Nobuyuki and the team presented at the conference on four main themes: Screen sharing using Copilot Add-on Store NVDA Coach New Forms of Learning with NVDA

They wrote to advise us that the event was a huge success, and they had around 100 people in attendance at their presentation. They sent us photographs and a link to their video presentation:

The Video is in Japanese, and includes a message from NV Access Training & Support manager Quentin Christensen (in English).

A banner from the NVDA Japanese Team session titled “NVDAではじめる、新しい「学び」のかたち” (“A New Form of ‘Learning’ Starting with NVDA”), presented at Sight World 2026 in Tokyo.

Unassigned gestures The last couple of releases I’ve highlighted the unassigned gestures, so let’s do that again. Unassigned gestures are things which you can do with a keystroke or touch action etc, but we didn’t set one up by default. There are only two this time around: Magnifier: A new unassigned command has been added to move the mouse cursor to the center of the magnified view. Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to the next/previous clickable element in browse mode.

The magnifier command is thanks to Cyrille, and the clickable one thanks to Cary. Thank you to them and ALL of our amazing NVDA community contributors!

One of the fixes in NVDA 2026.3.1 is with reporting switching Windows in Windows 10. I was thinking of writing a post on using alt+tab and the other ways of switching Windows – there are a few! But I realised, I already wrote a piece on switching Windows .

I’d forgotten about alt+escape ; I’m going to get back into using that! But that got me thinking about other general Windows keystrokes we might not know or (like me) might have forgotten. Another recent fix in NVDA (from NVDA 2026.3) is with File Explorer, so I thought we’d have a look at a couple of shortcuts which are well worth knowing, and some you may find useful:

Firstly, to start File Explorer, press Windows+e Open a new File Explorer window (from within File Explorer), with control+n

Navigating Move to next area: tab Move to previous area: shift+tab The focus starts in the “Items view list” – the contents of the currently selected folder. From here: Press shift+tab once to the folder list (you had to press it twice in some versions). Press tab to the “Split button” which is the name of the field the item list is sorted on. Once on the split button, use the arrows to select a field and enter or space to sort on it – if you select the same field, it will reverse the sort).

When in the items list view, you can customise the view. Windows provides shortcuts for the various views: control+shift+1 : Extra-large icons control+shift+2 : Large icons control+shift+3 : Medium icons control+shift+4 : Small icons control+shift+5 : List view control+shift+6 : Details view control+shift+7 : Tiles control+shift+8 : Content Note that in some versions of Windows (such as recent builds of Windows 11) these shortcuts do NOT work, but control+ALT+number works, for instance control+alt+6 for details view. The “details” view is the one I would personally recommend, as everything is in one list, and you get the most information about each item (file type, size, date modified etc) and can sort on any of those fields as needed. In details view, use the up and down arrow keys to move through the list. In most other view types, e.g. the icons views, use the left and right arrow keys .

Tabs Like browsers, you can have multiple folders open in different tabs or different windows: New blank tab: control+t Move to next tab: control+tab Move to previous tab: control+shift+tab

I cannot find a keystroke to open the current folder in a new tab. If you know one, please let me know! In the meantime, the following would work: Press shift+f6 once from the folder list to move to the tab control list. Press the applications key (or shift+f10 ) to open the context menu. Press the up arrow once to “Duplicate tab”. Press enter to open a new tab with the current folder.

To close a tab without closing all the other tabs, press control+w .

Address bar Move the focus to the address bar: alt+d . On the address bar, you can type the name of the folder or paste it from elsewhere, then press enter to load that folder.

Windows has several special folders. If you email us for help with an issue, we might ask you to send us your NVDA log, which you can find in your %temp% folder. To get to your %temp% folder: In File Explorer, press alt+d to go to the address bar Type: %temp% (That is, the word ‘temp’ with a percent sign either side) Press enter Windows will load a folder such as C:\Users\YourName\AppData\Local\Temp which is where it is storing your temporary files. There are others such as %onedrive% for your OneDrive folder (if setup), as well as system folders which are worth being careful around.

File properties One other quirk in File Explorer is opening file properties. In the file list, once you have located a file, press alt+enter to open the file properties for that file. This only works from the file list, even though you can access “ Properties ” in the context menu on folders in the folder list and it notes the alt+enter shortcut.

That’s all for this fortnight. We’ll be back towards the end of the month with more news, tips and tricks. I’m not sure what will be in that edition, but after all those lists of things in the file manager section, I’m going to aim for zero lists next fortnight – keep an eye out for that to see if I can do it!

Do keep the conversation going in the NVDA users email group , and remember, if you’d like to receive this blog by email, you can! Just go to https://www.nvaccess.org/newsletter and you can sign up for the blog, for details as new versions of NVDA drop, and more.

news.title: Navia: AI Accessible Map
news.summary: Navia is a touchable offline map for blind and low-vision people. Slide a finger across the screen and Navia speaks the street, shop, or place…
news.body:
Published 12 November 2026 by Mohammad

Navia is a touchable offline map for blind and low-vision people. Slide a finger across the screen and Navia speaks the street, shop, or place under your finger: its name, what it is, how far away it is, and directions as clock positions (for example, “2 o’clock, 40 meters”), following the way O&M training teaches. Sweeping around the map lets you build a mental picture of an area before you go there.

Safety note: Navia is an extra aid only. Always use a cane, guide dog, or another safe mobility method first.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

I am the developer. Navia was designed around TalkBack from the start rather than adapted afterwards. All buttons and controls are labelled and every dialog can be read with TalkBack.

The map itself is explored by touch: with TalkBack on, sliding a finger over the map speaks what is under it, and double-tap opens a menu of actions for that place (aim, hear its sounds, open in Google Maps, add to favourites). Voice dictation is available for search, adding points and renaming places.

For low vision there is an optional drawn map with a different marker shape per kind of place (not colour alone), street labels and a light/dark theme; it can turn itself off while TalkBack is running. Tested with Google TalkBack, including automated tests that run with real TalkBack enabled.

Known limitations: AI place recognition is experimental, needs a one-time ~240 MB model download and can miss a place; map quality depends on OpenStreetMap coverage in your area. Feedback is very welcome.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

Navia 1.1.12. Android 15

news.title: Una retina artificial convierte la luz infrarroja en señales eléctricas para estimular las neuronas del ojo
news.summary: Una investigación publicada en Nature Electronics presenta un implante retiniano capaz de transformar la luz infrarroja cercana en impulsos eléctricos. El dispositivo ha conseguido generar respuestas neuronales en ratones con degeneración de la retina y abre nuevas posibilidades para el desarrollo de prótesis visuales. La ingeniería biomédica continúa explorando nuevas formas de recuperar parcialmente la […] La entrada Una retina artificial convierte la luz infrarroja en señales eléctricas para estimular las neuronas del ojo se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
Una investigación publicada en Nature Electronics presenta un implante retiniano capaz de transformar la luz infrarroja cercana en impulsos eléctricos. El dispositivo ha conseguido generar respuestas neuronales en ratones con degeneración de la retina y abre nuevas posibilidades para el desarrollo de prótesis visuales.

La ingeniería biomédica continúa explorando nuevas formas de recuperar parcialmente la percepción visual en personas con enfermedades degenerativas de la retina. Una de las últimas investigaciones en este campo propone una solución basada en una retina artificial capaz de transformar la luz infrarroja cercana en señales eléctricas que estimulan directamente las neuronas del ojo.

El trabajo, publicado en abril de 2026 en la revista científica Nature Electronics , ha sido desarrollado por investigadores de distintas instituciones de Corea del Sur. Su propuesta combina sensores fotosensibles, microelectrodos de metal líquido y un sistema electrónico implantable que permite activar determinadas células de la retina.

Los experimentos realizados en ratones, incluidos animales con degeneración retiniana, han demostrado que el dispositivo puede provocar respuestas neuronales ante estímulos de luz infrarroja.

La visión natural comienza cuando los fotorreceptores de la retina, conocidos como conos y bastones, detectan la luz y la transforman en señales eléctricas. Estas señales se procesan en diferentes capas retinianas y posteriormente se transmiten al cerebro a través del nervio óptico.

Sin embargo, enfermedades como la retinosis pigmentaria provocan la degeneración progresiva de los fotorreceptores. Aunque estas células pueden llegar a desaparecer, otras estructuras de la retina, como las células ganglionares, pueden conservar parte de su funcionalidad.

La nueva tecnología pretende aprovechar precisamente esta capacidad.

El implante incorpora una matriz de fototransistores sensibles a la luz infrarroja cercana. Estos pequeños componentes detectan la radiación y generan una respuesta eléctrica que se transmite a través de unos microelectrodos situados en contacto con las neuronas retinianas.

De esta manera, el dispositivo evita depender de los fotorreceptores dañados y utiliza una vía alternativa para transmitir información visual al cerebro.

Uno de los aspectos más innovadores de esta investigación es el material empleado para fabricar los electrodos.

Los investigadores han desarrollado unos pequeños pilares tridimensionales de metal líquido, elaborados a partir de una aleación de galio e indio. Su estructura flexible permite adaptarse mejor a la superficie irregular de la retina y establecer un contacto más cercano con las células ganglionares.

Esta característica es importante porque los electrodos rígidos convencionales pueden generar problemas cuando se implantan en tejidos biológicos tan delicados.

Además, los extremos de estos microelectrodos incorporan nanopartículas de platino que mejoran la transmisión de carga eléctrica y facilitan la estimulación neuronal.

El dispositivo también incluye un filtro óptico ultrafino, de aproximadamente 360 nanómetros de grosor, diseñado para permitir el paso de determinadas longitudes de onda infrarrojas y controlar la entrada de luz visible en los sensores.

Para comprobar el funcionamiento de esta retina artificial, el equipo realizó diferentes experimentos tanto en tejidos retinianos aislados como en animales vivos.

Las pruebas incluyeron ratones sanos y ratones con degeneración retiniana, utilizados como modelo experimental de ceguera asociada a la pérdida de fotorreceptores.

Los investigadores observaron que, cuando el dispositivo recibía luz infrarroja cercana, los fototransistores generaban impulsos eléctricos capaces de activar las células ganglionares.

Además, mediante registros de actividad cerebral y pruebas de comportamiento, comprobaron que los estímulos llegaban hasta la corteza visual de los animales.

Uno de los resultados más relevantes fue que los ratones con degeneración retiniana también mostraron respuestas ante la estimulación infrarroja. Esto indica que el sistema puede aprovechar determinadas neuronas que permanecen funcionales incluso cuando los fotorreceptores han sufrido un deterioro importante.

Los estudios de biocompatibilidad también mostraron resultados iniciales favorables. En los animales evaluados durante seis meses no se observaron signos relevantes de inflamación o deterioro del tejido asociados al implante.

La investigación podría abrir una nueva vía para desarrollar prótesis visuales destinadas a personas que han perdido los fotorreceptores como consecuencia de enfermedades degenerativas de la retina.

En patologías como la retinosis pigmentaria, la pérdida progresiva de conos y bastones puede provocar una reducción importante de la visión e incluso llegar a causar ceguera.

Sin embargo, las células ganglionares y otras neuronas internas pueden permanecer relativamente conservadas durante determinadas fases de la enfermedad.

La propuesta de los investigadores consiste en aprovechar esas estructuras para transmitir información mediante estimulación eléctrica, sin depender de los fotorreceptores originales.

Otro aspecto interesante es que el dispositivo trabaja con luz infrarroja cercana, una región del espectro electromagnético que el ojo humano no puede percibir de forma natural. Esto permitiría crear un canal artificial de percepción que complemente la visión visible que todavía conserve la persona.

Los investigadores también plantean que esta tecnología podría adaptarse en el futuro para detectar otras longitudes de onda, aunque todavía es necesario estudiar sus posibilidades.

A pesar de los resultados obtenidos, esta retina artificial todavía se encuentra en una fase experimental.

Los ensayos se han realizado en ratones y no existen resultados que permitan afirmar que el dispositivo pueda utilizarse ya en personas con retinosis pigmentaria u otras enfermedades degenerativas.

Antes de plantear su aplicación clínica será necesario estudiar su seguridad a largo plazo, mejorar su miniaturización, reducir el consumo energético y comprobar su estabilidad después de periodos prolongados de implantación.

También será fundamental investigar cómo se traduce la estimulación eléctrica en una percepción visual útil para las personas. Activar las neuronas retinianas no significa recuperar automáticamente una visión natural.

No obstante, el trabajo publicado en Nature Electronics representa un avance relevante en el desarrollo de prótesis visuales y demuestra cómo la combinación de microelectrónica y materiales biocompatibles puede abrir nuevas posibilidades para intervenir sobre el sistema visual.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente: Nature

news.title: Clicklet
news.summary: Clicklet lets the Camera Control button on your iPhone start your Apple Shortcuts. Pick one shortcut to launch with a press, or turn on Menu mode and choose from a few favorites each time. Clicklet opens Apple Shortcuts to run your workflow, so you'll see the usual Shortcuts screens, along with any permission prompts or app handoffs your shortcut needs. To set up your library, install the included Connect Clicklet helper. It brings in your shortcut names and small icon images, which appear in your library, in the menu, and while a shortcut opens. You can also search for a shortcut or type its name. If you used an earlier version, replace the old helper with the new one and refresh to get icons. From the menu, tap Configure to go back to setup. You can scroll the menu by dragging along its side margins. Your shortcut names, icons and selections stay on your device. There's no account, advertising, analytics, subscription or in-app purchase. Camera access supports the Camera Control and lock-screen handoff and shows a live preview; Clicklet doesn't save photos or videos. Launching while your iPhone is locked requires authentication. Requires iOS 18 or later and Apple's Shortcuts app. Launching from the button requires an iPhone with Camera Control; set Clicklet in Settings > Camera > Camera Control. Opening Clicklet on its own shows your setup without running a shortcut.

news.body:
Published 11 November 2026 by Tommi Drophouse

Sight Buddy is a free, open-source Android app for asking questions about images and text. Once the models are downloaded, it works offline with no account, subscription, or usage limit.

It can chat about images and text, find the right page in a document, and share, save, or copy text. The app recommends a model setup that fits the phone, so users do not need technical knowledge.

It is a new release with early users internationally, and user feedback has helped shape the design.
