news.title: Apple TV introduces new Sign Language interpretation feature
news.summary: Today, Apple announced a new accessibility feature on the Apple TV app offering sign language interpretation for supported titles.
news.body:
Text of this article

November 10, 2026

UPDATE

Apple TV introduces new Sign Language interpretation feature

New accessibility feature debuts Friday, November 13, with the streaming premiere of Being Heumann

Today, Apple announced a new accessibility feature for the Apple TV app that gives viewers the option to watch supported titles with accompanying sign language interpretation. 1 The feature will be available on Friday, November 13, alongside the global streaming premiere of Being Heumann , a film based on the true story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann, on Apple TV.

In addition to Being Heumann, interpretation for American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will be available for the movie F1. Later this year, Way of the Warrior Kid and Greyhound will follow, with more Apple Original titles to come. When turned on in Apple TV app settings, the Sign Language option will appear on supported Apple Original titles.

“At Apple, we believe everyone should be able to enjoy great stories and entertainment,” said Sarah Herrlinger, Apple’s senior director of Global Accessibility Policy and Initiatives. “Bringing sign language interpretation to Apple TV is an exciting step forward in making the viewing experience more accessible and inclusive for Deaf audiences. Accessibility is a core value at Apple, and we’re proud to continue creating experiences that allow more people to enjoy the content they love.”

Designed with Native Signers in the Deaf Community

Apple TV offers a sign language experience that’s designed and tested by Deaf and native signers. Each performance is carefully crafted to fit and complement the Apple Original film it interprets.

“It’s incredibly meaningful to see our beautiful language authentically represented onscreen,” said Daniel Durant, who appears in Being Heumann and directed the film’s sign language interpretation. “Bringing this experience to life required a lot of care to ensure every translation captured the emotion and meaning of the story. I’m proud to have been part of Being Heumann and thrilled to see Apple TV supporting greater accessibility for Deaf audiences.”

New Ways to Discover Titles with Sign Language

Titles with sign language interpretation will be labeled with a Sign Language icon, making it easy to know when the option is available. Viewers can enable the feature in Apple TV app settings, then press the Sign Language button while watching. Search will also make it easier to find titles that feature sign language with simple phrases like “with ASL.”

As sign language interpretation becomes more widely available across streaming services, the new “Movies & Shows with American Sign Language” collection on the Apple TV app will offer viewers a simple way to explore titles featuring sign language, in one dedicated destination.

Being Heumann

In Being Heumann , Judy Heumann (Ruth Madeley) — scrappy, defiant, and done being treated like a burden — turns her outrage into a revolution. In San Francisco in 1977, she and more than 100 disability rights protesters organize a sit-in to send a very loud message: The system is broken — not us. The film marks the second collaboration between Apple Original Films and writer-director Siân Heder, who directed the multi-Academy Award-winning film CODA, which made history as the first film with a predominantly Deaf cast to receive the Best Picture honor.

Being Heumann premieres globally on Apple TV on Friday, November 13. Viewers can add Being Heumann to their watchlist on Apple TV .

Apple TV offers premium, compelling drama and comedy series, feature films, groundbreaking documentaries, and kids and family entertainment, and is available to watch across all of a user’s favorite screens. After its launch on November 1, 2019, Apple TV became the first all-original streaming service to launch around the world, and has premiered more original hits and received more award recognitions faster than any other streaming service in its debut. To date, Apple Original films, documentaries, and series have been honored with 919 wins and 3,829 award nominations and counting, including Academy Award Best Picture winner CODA and Academy Award winner F1, the highest-grossing sports feature of all time.

About Apple TV

Apple TV is available on the Apple TV app in 170 countries and regions, on over 1 billion screens, including iPhone; iPad; Apple TV 4K; Apple Vision Pro; Mac; popular smart TVs from Samsung, LG, Sony, VIZIO, TCL, and others; Roku and Amazon Fire TV devices; Chromecast with Google TV; PlayStation and Xbox gaming consoles; and at tv.apple.com , for $14.99 per month with a seven-day free trial for new subscribers. For a limited time, customers who purchase and activate a new iPhone, iPad, Apple TV 4K, or Mac can enjoy three months of Apple TV for free. 2

For more information, visit apple.com/tvpr and see the full list of supported devices .

news.title: Cadence Tactile Tablet, la pantalla táctil que permite explorar gráficos, braille y vídeo en tiempo real
news.summary: El acceso a la información digital sigue planteando importantes barreras para las personas ciegas y con discapacidad visual. Aunque las líneas braille y los lectores de pantalla han facilitado considerablemente el uso de ordenadores y dispositivos electrónicos, determinados contenidos, como gráficos, mapas, imágenes o vídeos, continúan siendo difíciles de explorar de forma autónoma. En este […] La entrada Cadence Tactile Tablet, la pantalla táctil que permite explorar gráficos, braille y vídeo en tiempo real se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
El acceso a la información digital sigue planteando importantes barreras para las personas ciegas y con discapacidad visual. Aunque las líneas braille y los lectores de pantalla han facilitado considerablemente el uso de ordenadores y dispositivos electrónicos, determinados contenidos, como gráficos, mapas, imágenes o vídeos, continúan siendo difíciles de explorar de forma autónoma.

En este contexto surge Cadence Tactile Tablet , un dispositivo desarrollado por la empresa estadounidense Tactile Engineering que propone una nueva forma de interactuar con los contenidos digitales: una pantalla táctil dinámica capaz de representar texto en braille, gráficos e incluso imágenes en movimiento.

A diferencia de las líneas braille tradicionales, que presentan los caracteres de forma secuencial en una única línea, Cadence incorpora una superficie formada por pequeños puntos móviles que pueden elevarse y descender para representar información mediante el tacto.

Su pantalla dispone de 384 puntos táctiles , distribuidos en 48 celdas braille de ocho puntos, organizadas en cuatro líneas de doce celdas. Esta configuración permite consultar varias líneas de texto simultáneamente y explorar representaciones gráficas sin depender exclusivamente de descripciones verbales.

El dispositivo utiliza tecnología MEMS ( Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems ), basada en sistemas microelectromecánicos, para controlar el movimiento de los puntos táctiles. Según el fabricante, estos pueden actualizarse hasta tres veces por segundo, permitiendo modificar la información que aparece bajo los dedos.

Una de las características más llamativas de Cadence es su capacidad para representar gráficos táctiles dinámicos. Esto significa que la superficie no se limita a mostrar una imagen estática, sino que puede modificar los puntos en tiempo real para transmitir información cambiante.

Entre sus posibilidades destacan:

Una demostración especialmente llamativa tuvo lugar durante las 500 Millas de Indianápolis de 2026. Mediante Cadence, los aficionados ciegos pudieron seguir táctilmente el movimiento de los coches en el circuito, convirtiendo la información visual de la carrera en patrones que cambiaban bajo sus dedos.

Esta experiencia muestra cómo la tecnología táctil puede ampliar el acceso no solo a la lectura y al aprendizaje, sino también a acontecimientos deportivos y contenidos audiovisuales.

Otra de sus particularidades es su diseño modular. Cadence puede utilizarse como una unidad independiente o conectarse con otras unidades para ampliar la superficie táctil disponible.

El fabricante contempla configuraciones de hasta cuatro dispositivos conectados, que permiten trabajar con una superficie de mayor tamaño y representar contenidos más amplios.

Además, incorpora teclado braille tipo Perkins, controles direccionales y botones multifunción para navegar por los contenidos, seleccionar líneas, acceder a etiquetas y controlar diferentes aplicaciones.

La conexión con ordenadores y dispositivos compatibles se realiza mediante Bluetooth o USB-C. También dispone de software propio, CadenceOS, que permite gestionar el dispositivo y acceder a diferentes aplicaciones y contenidos.

Las aplicaciones de una pantalla táctil de estas características pueden ser especialmente interesantes en el ámbito educativo.

El acceso a mapas, gráficos matemáticos, representaciones científicas y otros recursos visuales constituye uno de los grandes retos de la educación inclusiva. Aunque existen materiales en relieve y herramientas de adaptación, su elaboración puede requerir tiempo, conocimientos especializados y recursos específicos.

Dispositivos como Cadence permiten explorar nuevas formas de presentar estos contenidos digitalmente, facilitando su actualización y ofreciendo posibilidades de interacción que no proporcionan los materiales táctiles estáticos.

También pueden contribuir al acceso a información que cambia constantemente, como gráficos estadísticos, retransmisiones deportivas o determinadas representaciones audiovisuales.

No obstante, es importante recordar que la disponibilidad de una pantalla táctil dinámica no garantiza por sí sola la accesibilidad de cualquier contenido. La distribución de los puntos, la complejidad de las representaciones y la necesidad de una adaptación comprensible siguen siendo aspectos fundamentales para que la información pueda interpretarse correctamente mediante el tacto.

Cadence Tactile Tablet representa una evolución interesante dentro de la tiflotecnología: pasar de dispositivos centrados principalmente en reproducir texto braille a superficies capaces de transmitir información espacial y dinámica.

Su desarrollo abre nuevas posibilidades para la lectura, la educación, la comunicación y el acceso a contenidos digitales. También plantea una cuestión importante de cara al futuro: cómo conseguir que las imágenes, los gráficos y otros contenidos diseñados originalmente para la vista puedan convertirse en experiencias táctiles realmente comprensibles y accesibles.

La tecnología todavía tiene retos por delante, pero propuestas como esta muestran que el futuro de la accesibilidad digital también pasa por ampliar las posibilidades del sentido del tacto.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente: Tactile Engineering , Double Tap Live .

news.title: NoteTell Money Reader
news.summary: NoteTell Money Reader is designed to help people who are blind or have low vision identify bills in real time. Simply point the iPhone camera at the bill you want to identify, then hear, feel, or see its value. If you’re blind, have low vision, or are deafblind, NoteTell Money Reader lets you identify bills without any assistance. While shopping, use NoteTell to check your money at the checkout and make sure you get the right change back. You can also use NoteTell to quickly sort your money at home. NoteTell doesn’t require an internet connection, so it identifies bills anywhere, at any time. NoteTell can identify bills at any angle. It is designed to work with bills that are folded, creased, worn, or partly in view. NoteTell is designed to work indoors, outdoors, and even in total darkness. When your environment is too dark to identify bills, NoteTell turns the flashlight on automatically. Vibration Mode tells you the value of each bill as vibrations in your hand—without anyone else hearing it. Each bill has its own vibration pattern. The lowest bill has one pulse, and each higher bill has one more. Pulses come in pairs, so they’re easier to count. Vibration Mode is also useful in noisy places and for people who are deafblind. When VoiceOver is on, double-tap with two fingers to switch between Speech Mode and Vibration Mode. For users with low vision, NoteTell shows the value of each bill in large, high-contrast numbers on the screen. You can complete every task in NoteTell Money Reader using only VoiceOver, without sighted assistance. If you use a braille display with VoiceOver, you can use NoteTell to get the value of each bill in real time. Ask Siri, “Identify currency with NoteTell,” to use NoteTell hands-free. You can also add NoteTell to Control Center or the Lock Screen, assign it to the Action button, or set it up as a Vocal Shortcut. With the full version, you can use Currency Conversion to hear each bill’s value in your home currency when you travel. NoteTell uses on-device processing to identify bills, which means your data never leaves your iPhone. Camera images are never stored on the device or on any servers. You can try the full version free for 14 days. You won’t be charged when the trial ends. You can continue using NoteTell for free to identify the lowest notes of each currency. The full version is also available as a one-time purchase. And with Family Sharing, up to five other people can enjoy your purchase too.

news.title: Apple Releases Version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS with Bug Fixes and Security Updates
news.summary: Apple has today released version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS, bringing bug fixes and security updates, including for a vulnerability that allowed macOS command line tools to use compromised eMudhra certificates. As the 27.2.1 updates were not distributed to external testers prior to their release, we do not have any information on whether they contain any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as these updates appear to have been released to address a small number of specific issues, we do not expect them to contain any such fixes. Release Notes iOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your iPhone. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . iPadOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your iPad. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your Mac. watchOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your Apple Watch. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . How to Update iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 are available over-the-air (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if updating OTA, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update. To install macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Update Now button to begin the update process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. watchOS 27.2.1 is available over-the-air (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.

news.title: Llega TCA DjMix 1.0: 🧑‍🦯 DJ accesible para Windows!
news.summary: Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va?
news.body:
Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va?

Después de bastante tiempo trabajando en un proyecto nuevo y distinto dentro de la familia TCA Software, ¡por fin llega TCA DjMix 1.0!

Si eres de los que creció viendo a algún DJ mezclar pistas con fundidos suaves y sincronizando beats al milisegundo… pues este es tu programa. Y lo mejor: está diseñado desde cero para que cualquiera pueda usarlo con lector de pantalla.

Sí, lo has leído bien. TCA DjMix es la primera aplicación de DJ accesible para Windows pensada específicamente para quienes usamos NVDA, JAWS o Narrador. Pero no es solo para nosotros: cualquier persona puede usarla con teclado, con ratón o incluso con una controladora MIDI.

Y esto tiene algo todavía más especial: este es el primer programa de toda la familia TCA Software que fue construido usando Inteligencia Artificial. Sí, justo como lo lees. Por primera vez en la historia de TCA Software, creamos un programa "by coding" con ayuda de IA.

TCA DjMix es una aplicación de mezcla musical accesible que reúne todo lo necesario para crear tus sesiones. Estas son sus funciones clave:

• Biblioteca unificada y platos independientes

TCA DjMix incluye una biblioteca centralizada donde cargas tu carpeta de música, la cual se navega 100% con lector de pantalla y lista todos los archivos automáticamente (formatos compatibles: WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 y AIFF). Desde esa misma lista puedes cargar las pistas de manera independiente en el plato 1 o en el plato 2 usando los atajos (Alt+1 o Alt+2), controlando el volumen y la reproducción de cada plato por separado.

• Sincronización automática de BPM (Beatmatch)

El Beatmatch automático analiza ambas pistas y ajusta sus tempos para que se sincronicen solos. Ideal para quienes están empezando y no quieren complicarse ajustando a mano.

• Crossfader accesible

El crossfader permite hacer fundidos suaves entre los dos platos, tal como lo hacen los DJ profesionales. Se puede controlar cómodamente desde el teclado o con el ratón.

• Efectos de sonido (Samples)

Puedes agregar efectos como scratches, fades o hits con un solo atajo de teclado. Solo hay que poner los archivos WAV de efectos en la carpeta "samples" y ya están listos para sonar.

• Compatible con controladoras MIDI (funcionalidad en versión prueba).

Si tienes una controladora Pioneer DDJ-400, DDJ-SR o DDJ-SR2, TCA DjMix la detecta automáticamente. No hace falta configurar nada: conéctala y empieza a mezclar usando los controles físicos que ya conoces.

Algunos de los atajos más prácticos para controlar todo con el teclado:

• Ctrl+L: Abrir carpeta y cargar música en la biblioteca.

• Alt+1 / Alt+2: Cargar pista seleccionada en el plato 1 o plato 2.

• F5 / F6: Reproducir o pausar el plato 1 / plato 2.

• F7 / F8: Detener el plato 1 / plato 2.

• Tab: Recorrer controles.

• Ctrl+B: Sincronizar el plato activo con el otro plato.

• Ctrl+F1 a Ctrl+F12: Reproducir samples del banco actual.

• Ctrl+S: Detener todos los samples.

• Ctrl+M: Iniciar o detener la automezcla.

• Ctrl+P: Abrir la configuración.

• Ctrl+J: Panel de controladora MIDI.

TCA DjMix está pensado para cualquier persona interesada en la mezcla musical, pero especialmente para personas ciegas o con baja visión que usan lectores de pantalla y que siempre soñaron con hacer una mezcla como un DJ profesional. Con los atajos correctos y un poco de práctica, cualquiera puede manejarlo sin necesidad de ver la pantalla.

Y hablando de práctica... ¡te lo ponemos muy fácil! Más abajo, en esta misma entrada, te dejamos el tutorial en audio y vídeo donde puedes ver y escuchar el programa en acción paso a paso.

El programa es compatible con: • Windows 10 X64.

• Windows 11.

• TCA DjMix 1.0 se distribuye como un archivo ZIP descargable. Incluye todo lo necesario: el ejecutable, los samples predeterminados y las instrucciones. No requiere instalación, simplemente descomprime y ejecuta.

• Es multilenguaje: español, italiano, inglés y portugués.

• En algunos PC, podrían necesitar la instalación de las librerías Visual Estudio C++ (en la descarga estarán).

Les dejaré en la descarga:

• El audio tutorial (en los canales Odysse y YouTube estará en video tutorial).

• El programa: TCA DjMix 1.0.

• Archivo con las librerías Visual Estudio C++.

TCA DjMix es una herramienta que demuestra que la accesibilidad en la tecnología musical no tiene por qué ser un sueño imposible. Con un diseño pensado desde cero para lectores de pantalla, soporte para controladoras MIDI reales y funciones profesionales como beatmatch automático y efectos de sonido, este programa abre las puertas del mundo DJ a personas que antes tenían dificultades para acceder a estas herramientas.

Y lo más bonito: nació del esfuerzo dentro de la familia TCA Software, que ahora además cuenta con IA como herramienta de desarrollo. ¿Quién dice que no se puede?

¡Los leo en los comentarios! Cualquier duda, sugerencia o historia contándome cómo usaron TCA DjMix, no duden en escribirme.

¡Un abrazo y buena música!

news.body:
Tras una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión contiene un parche que resuelve incidencias de seguridad. También corrige un fallo introducido en NVDA 2026.3 con el conmutador de tareas de Windows 10. Se ha restaurado la voz de Espeak NG en portugués de Brasil al comportamiento que tenía en NVDA 2026.2. Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3.1, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es 6f80a5b0ca720a7d0d314b5be212f37388bbe81a1107ac3298c1821a1cd3f052. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

news.title: How To Route Screen Reader Audio To Different Devices With Sandfly Screen Reader
news.summary: There is no need to explain why a screen reader user might sometimes want to have the screen reader’s audio routed to a different audio…
news.body:
Published 8 November 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

There is no need to explain why a screen reader user might sometimes want to have the screen reader’s audio routed to a different audio device than the default one.

On Android, this is not natively possible. Samsung’s One UI offers a workaround through the Separate App Sound feature, which gets the job done, even if it is not perfect. However, to my knowledge, other OEMs do not offer a comparable feature.

TalkBack, Android’s default built-in screen reader, does not offer a similar capability either. Sandfly , an open-source screen reader, allows users to change the device used to output the screen reader’s speech and audio. It also provides an option to route the audio to the phone’s speaker when specific audio devices are connected.

Sandfly is not the only screen reader that provides this feature. Another screen reader that offers similar functionality is Backtalk , and other screen readers might have something similar. However, this post only covers how to use the audio output feature found in Sandfly. Note that setting up Sandfly is outside the scope of this post.

Open Sandfly settings. You can access them from the Sandfly menu or by selecting Sandfly from the list of installed accessibility services. You can also access the settings by selecting the app from the apps list.

Find “Audio output” and activate it.

Then, press “Audio output device” to see a list of currently available audio devices, including System Default, Phone Speaker, and connected wired and wireless audio devices.

Select any device to route Sandfly’s audio through it.

To have the audio come out of the phone’s speaker when a certain device is connected, choose “Phone speaker with these devices” and check all the devices you want. Whenever one of the selected devices is connected, Sandfly’s audio will come out of the phone’s speaker instead of the connected device.

Use the “Keep speech on the phone while casting” option to determine whether you want the screen reader’s audio to come out of the phone’s speaker when you cast your screen.

Although Sandfly is not my primary screen reader at the moment, I tested Audio Output and was impressed by the reliability of the audio routing. I was able to switch between Bluetooth headphones, wired USB-C earbuds, and the phone’s speakers without any issues or interference with media playback. This is consistent with tests conducted by other team members, including full-time Sandfly users.

Published in Tips and Tricks Tutorials

news.title: The Day Bingo Went to Brent Cross, Met the iPhone Duo, and Bought a Pizza
news.summary: Introduction Dear old Brent Cross has featured quite heavily in my life. When I was a child, it was a brand spanking new shopping centre, famed for being absolutely enormous as well as the first attempt outside London to bring shopping and entertainment together. London had its west end, and we in north London had our north-west end in Brent Cross. My family, certain of whom have a worrying fixation with shopping trips, used to love it. Later in life, Brent Cross was where I went to get my wedding suit made. Note, dear gentleman readers, that I had my suit made, not hired, and and you should not allow yourselves to be wed in someone else's clothes either. After all, is the bride going to hire her wedding dress? Brent Cross is also where our Apple Store is, and last Saturday I persuaded Mrs Bingo to come along with me and meet the new iPhone line-up. Now, notwithstanding I've been to Brent Cross many times, I've never been on a Saturday afternoon. Don't! It's phenomenally busy and immediately put pay to the idea that I might capture a nice, atmospheric audio review of my iPhone explorations. Audio there is, but it is unfit for human consumption. Plus, although we've both been to the Apple Store there a couple of times, we had forgotten where it was. Cue a quarter of an hour wandering around past every chain store imaginable alongside coffee shops and a pop-up pizzeria, which admittedly we noted down as a place to visit on the way out, we finally remembered it was on the upper level and got there in in the end. It was the work of a moment to find a demo iPhone Duo model with which to play, safely cabled to the counter as a countermeasure to light-fingered iProdders. Let the games begin, as they say. What This Review is, and What it Ain't I want to kick off by setting some parameters. These are my unfiltered impressions. I'm not a tech journalist so I'll not be getting down and dirty with the processing power or what have you. I'm also assuming you're someone who either has the budget for the duo or who is at least very curious and perhaps wishes they had. So I'll be entirely subjective about whether it's worth the money—ultimately, that's a value judgement for each and every one of us. There may be a bit of repetition if you're familiar with other iPhone Duo pioneers' output, like the excellent Dave Nason's contributions, and if that happens it's purely coincidental, and a byproduct of my giving you my unfiltered impressions. But I have tried to keep this to a minimum and I also cross-refer to Dave's contribution, so please look at that if you haven't already. For you braillists out there, you'll be pleased to learn I did get a good go at BSI. Still reading? Thank gawd for that! A Jet-Setter's Passport Those who say the Duo is like a passport are not wrong. It really is more or less the same size and shape. I'm not talking a passport that most people have, however. I mean a passport like my mate Penguin has, because he is sent to so many foreign parts by his employer. In the UK, we have a choice of adding a good few extra pages to our passport if we're like Penguin. the Duo's like Penguin's passport, so a bit thicker than mine. Never mind Penguin, Bingo! How does it feel in the hand? Honestly? Fantastic. Size, weight, everything. I can't fault it. True, I couldn't test it in the pocket as I suspect various alarms would have gone off and I did not have a pocket at quite the right height what with its being cabled to the table and all that lark, but I could tell there'd be no trouble fitting it in any but the smallest of pockets. Dave Nason has commented on the weight. I have to say, I didn't find this at all noticeable. It is, perhaps, the weight of a wallet with a reasonable number of coins in it. That's what it feels like to hold. Not a wallet stuffed full to the seams, but a wallet with a handful of change in it. I say that on the assumption that anyone can still remember what carrying cash was like. Now, I admit I didn't hold it in my hand for very long, whereas Dave has actually been using one; but even allowing for that I was not at all concerned. Sure, it's heavier than an iPhone Air, but that's what you expect. Know When to Fold Up Dave has covered this in some detail already. For my part, I found the magnetic snap as the Duo folded very satisfying. The thing looks a very robust piece of kit when folded. When unfolded, in small tablet mode, it still feels solid—not unlike the 9.4in iPad Pro I used to own. Like Dave, I could feel the crease at the centre point but not unpleasantly so, and it does serve as a very handy orientation point. For me, and accidental though this benefit may be, I preferred it to the iPad because of this. Sound as a Pound I was in a very busy Apple Store, so bear that in mind. Additionally, the only settings I changed were to enable BSI's quick activation gesture. I played no music and listened to no books. In unfolded landscape, I would say it was, though if you're in the market for a Pro and you have a 16 Pro Max like I do, I would immediately agree that the 18 Pro is a big step up from that, and worth it for the audio alone. I tried typing as fast as the cable on the table would allow in a blank note in the notes app and made hardly any errors. Those I did make were down to the unfortunate stoop I had to adopt owing to the cable on the table aforesaid, compounded by Voiceover's being set to speak both characters and words—I had forgotten how utterly tiresome I find that much keyboard echo and how it appears to slow one down. I then folded the phone and tried it in Screen Away Mode. All I can say is the speed of my Landscape tabletop typing was blasted out of the water. Again, I tried to braille as fast as I could and I can't remember making any errors. For me, these features don't matter. If they matter to you, the Duo's not your bag. Our friend was also very forthcoming on durability and battery. The battery, said he, is up with the Pro in his experience if you use it folded most of the time. unfolded, you will obviously get less. To the extent that some people say you get a lot less, well all I can say (and our friend agreed with me) is that the novelty of being able to fold and unfold our diplomatic passport of a Duo means one's likely to do it rather a lot to begin with. They are not deep pan but are decent Italian bases. The author can attest that they are an ideal snack en route out of the shopping centre. One slice will keep you going just fine.

Later in life, Brent Cross was where I went to get my wedding suit made. Note, dear gentleman readers, that I had my suit made, not hired, and and you should not allow yourselves to be wed in someone else's clothes either.
